id.description: Unique. Also the file name in exported bundles.

updated.description: When the document last changed in substance. Policies match the 'Last updated' line in their text.

created.description: When the content was first written, from its real source (a file, a commit, or a page), not when it moved into the corpus.

pdf.description: True when the knowledge area offers it as a download.

edition.description: The document's edition, such as 1.0. Raise the minor number for clarifications, the major number when a promise or rule changes. Printed on PDFs.

audience.description: Who it's written for, in a few words, such as "Owners and office managers".

related.description: Ids of other documents a reader may want next. Each must exist.

example_of.description: Example: the id of the blank template or form it fills in.

fictional.description: Example: true when the people and business in it are invented. Consumers label it as fiction.

reviewed.description: Comparison: when the outside facts in it, such as prices and features, were last checked.

origin.description: Where the text came from before the corpus held it.

published.description: The live URL that shows this document, if any.

key.description: Short name a consumer uses for anchors, such as case-<key> on the site.

order.description: Position within its type when a consumer shows a set, such as the case study rail.

stat_key.description: Case study: the headline result, shown in bold.

stat.description: Case study: the rest of the result line after the headline.

short_needs.description: Case study: one line on the problem, for cards and the at-a-glance table.

short_execute.description: Case study: one line on what was done, for cards and the at-a-glance table.

short_observe.description: Case study: one line on how it was measured, for cards and the at-a-glance table.

short_normalize.description: Case study: one line on what happens next, for cards and the at-a-glance table.

x-types.$comment: Extra rules per type, checked by tools/lint.mjs. sections lists the H2 headings a document of that type must have, in order.

faq.$comment: Each H2 is a question and its text is the answer.

directive.$comment: How a consumer behaves rather than what it says about neon1, such as Neo's character and rules. Consumers keep it apart from the facts they answer from.

standard.$comment: How neon1 works: a habit or rule neon1 holds itself to, written as what it does, with the reason. Never a claim of certification or measured results.

guide.$comment: A how-to or use case for someone outside neon1. Says who it's for and what they'll be able to do.

template.$comment: A blank document to copy and fill in, such as a proposal. Blanks are four or more underscores; choices are - [ ] task items.

form.$comment: A blank record to fill in, such as a discovery record. Same blanks and checkboxes as a template.

example.$comment: A template or form filled in, so a reader can see what good looks like.

comparison.$comment: neon1 next to the alternatives: who each fits, where each is better, sources for every outside fact. The last section is Sources.
